rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Walk-away test (M2+)
rules_evaluated.evidence: L62-64 Phase 2 study prompt: 'This is a big read and will run a while. As you go, keep me posted every thirty seconds or so' — agent works independently while student steps back; matches walk-away shape even though not phrased as literal chair-leaving.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: 50% magic rule (M3-M8)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ratio is measured across the 6 post-M2 modules, not derivable from one exercise file in isolation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the agentic design, no human backstops
rules_evaluated.evidence: L7 hands the M5-done-or-stopped call to the student ('decide whether the M5 session is done enough...'); no 'Antti observes manually' style backstop anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Quality ladder tier target
rules_evaluated.evidence: Arc-peak tier assignment (should this land as a 9) is an editorial/portfolio call already recorded by prior judge passes in the Quality block (L103-105), not independently re-derivable from a single static read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: One exercise = one bounded activity, never sub-number
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase 1 and Phase 2 are not an artificially sub-numbered atomic do-observe-adjust-observe loop; each phase carries its own do/observe cycle. Closest call is whether the two phases should instead be split per §12 (assessed there).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Modules composable across variants, no forks
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is a single AE101-scoped exercise (worktrees, CLAUDE.local.md, engineer register); no VARIANT markers or audience fork present, none needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Three-level completeness
rules_evaluated.evidence: Runtime artifact trainer reads at blocker = Failure modes + Decision points (L156-171); sendable asset = the CLAUDE.local.md cut / observations / diagrams named at L91-93 'Decide what crosses back to your main repo'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Pattern-recognition LOs need n>=2 instances with contrast
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase 1's prompt (L27 fence) explicitly requires reading BOTH sessions with contrast ('what packaging caught... what packaging missed'); Phase 2 scans many sessions across projects for recurring shapes. Both clear n>=2-with-contrast.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Progression-with-variations is the spine
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer block L157 names the reused move explicitly: 'Echoes M5's Phase 1 diagnostic.' New face here is comparative (quoted moments from BOTH runs) vs M5's single-run diagnostic — a genuine new instantiation, not verbatim repeat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student agency, adults decide
rules_evaluated.evidence: Repeated opportunity-not-compulsion phrasing: L53 'How wide you look, and what you choose to map, is yours', L68 'How far you take this is yours', L60 blockquote 'Cut the scan whenever you like'. No forced-pacing imperatives found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Delegation: student brings, Claude screens
rules_evaluated.evidence: L62 prompt has Claude read sessions it has real filesystem access to (~/.claude/projects/) and explicitly hands off what it can't reach: 'If there are other repos you should look at that aren't in there, ask me where they are.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Split mega-exercise when phases = distinct skills + artifacts
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest-to-violating: L53 'Look wider than the two sessions' marks a real scope break between Phase 1 (task-specific diff) and Phase 2 (cross-project scan). Stays inside because both phases run in one continuous worktree session, share a single 35-min budget, and the maintainer 'Placement' line (L111) documents the split as deliberate, not accidental merge.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-realism check
rules_evaluated.evidence: Named artifacts (task.md, plan.md, ./CLAUDE.local.md, M5 worktree, git refs) were all established as prework by M4/M5 per L5-7; nothing new and unverifiable is invoked cold.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Teach principle + technique, default
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mermaid (L71,73) is Claude's own output format, not a technique the student must invoke or understand — no unexplained black-box action is asked of the student.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Auto-fire sim+eval after significant rewrite
rules_evaluated.evidence: Generation-time process rule; Quality block (L103-105) already logs a compendium audit + a targeted re-audit after a body change, evidencing the process fired historically. Not independently re-verifiable from this static read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions in prompts, not body prose
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 5 mandatory-or-optional student moves (diff, rule-cut, study, shapes, primitives) live in {{prompt:}} fences (L27,42,64,73,85); body sections (L29-38, L44-47, L58-60) carry only recovery/steering coaching, not the forcing functions themselves.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Corporate infra never a forcing function
rules_evaluated.evidence: No external/corporate tooling (MCP, shared repo, SSO) required anywhere in this file; entirely personal-machine work.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Personal-first, team promotion via human conversation
rules_evaluated.evidence: The rule cut (L40-42 prompt) targets ./CLAUDE.local.md directly, no auto-promotion to a shared/team file is suggested anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Measure silent failure, not just friction
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer 'Failure modes + diagnostics' (L156-160) names silent-failure shapes directly, e.g. 'Phase 1 packaging-over-credit ... if Phase 1 outputs zero misses, Claude is over-crediting' — a frictionless-but-wrong outcome, not just friction.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't pre-set categories before experiment runs
rules_evaluated.evidence: L62 prompt explicitly bans pre-specified categories: 'Group what you find by the kind of work it is ... Don't filter to what looks important. Show me what actually recurs, including the dull stuff.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verification layers sample different error distributions
rules_evaluated.evidence: Eval-architecture rule about the training's composite verification gate, not a per-exercise body-content check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cheap-before-expensive verification ordering
rules_evaluated.evidence: Eval-architecture tiering rule; not something a single exercise's student-facing body implements or violates.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rule in memory without forcing function = worse than no rule
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is the exercise's own subject matter: L40-42 prompt forces the cut ('Find the one rule ... Cut it ... Show me the line you cut'), not a passive memory note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Short skeptical pushback = re-verify trigger
rules_evaluated.evidence: L46-47 'Push back if the diff touches more than the one rule you flagged' is exactly this pattern: re-open and re-check rather than re-confirm.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cohort execution trainer-paced + concurrent
rules_evaluated.evidence: 35-min budget (20+15, L19,L51) is stated per-phase not as a naive trainer-time+student-time sum; nothing in body contradicts concurrent pacing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Host-skill optional; maintainer blocks trainer-only
rules_evaluated.evidence: No host-skill referenced anywhere. Maintainer block names the actor correctly: L158 'Trainer push: "name one thing the verifier missed, concretely..."'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats in-chat over file-write
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reflective file-write-with-no-reader is introduced; the only file write is the real CLAUDE.local.md rule cut (L40-42), which has a genuine downstream reader (the student's own future sessions).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom default; no authored room-management cues
rules_evaluated.evidence: No group/pair/discuss-with-neighbor language anywhere in the body; this is entirely solo work, consistent with the default.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Eval = fixed yardstick
rules_evaluated.evidence: Eval-loop architecture rule; not applicable to a student-facing exercise body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reading burden for verification banned; Claude audits Claude
rules_evaluated.evidence: L31 'Push back where Claude generalises... re-run the prompt with the quote rule re-asserted' asks the student to notice a shape-level gap (missing quote), not to manually verify deep correctness of a diff — the light generalization-catch pushback this training has taught as a repeated skill since M1, not the deep Claude-on-Claude verification work the rule bans offloading to humans.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-report + self-audit charity
rules_evaluated.evidence: L40-42 rule-cut prompt requires Claude to show the actual cut line and justify it ('Show me the line you cut, in two sentences why'), giving the student an artifact to check rather than trusting a bare summary claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Offered structures need forced-engagement mechanic
rules_evaluated.evidence: The rule-cut prompt (L40-42) forces justification before acceptance rather than handing a takeable-verbatim default; no offered-defaults-copied-unedited pattern present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Source-type blindness on ingestion
rules_evaluated.evidence: No heterogeneous slide/PDF source-folder ingestion in this exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Task selection drives outcome, name floor AND ceiling
rules_evaluated.evidence: This exercise has no student task-selection step (the task is already fixed as 'the same task from M4/M5').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer hedge naming section's own failure mode = cut signal
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: Mood target Watch-for (L113) 'compliance-feel ... or credibility-performance'. Premise-test: removing the hedge, the Mood target section still stands as a defensible statement of intended experience — it's a trainer risk-note, not a speculation propping up an otherwise-indefensible claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audience tier determines authoring substrate
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 engineer tier authors via CLAUDE.local.md directly (L40-42), matching the rule's 'authored plugins + multi-layer CLAUDE.md' substrate for this audience.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verification machinery needs smoke-test before trust
rules_evaluated.evidence: No new verification machinery (hook, judge, Ralph loop) is built in this exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Context-loading tiers as staged progression
rules_evaluated.evidence: CLAUDE.local.md auto-load tier was established in earlier modules; this file reuses it without newly revealing a tier.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Removals are strategic, ask before cutting
rules_evaluated.evidence: Generation-time constraint on the author making edits, not a property the finished student-facing body exhibits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Symmetric visible-mechanics > runtime fork under dual-runtime constraint
rules_evaluated.evidence: File only exercises the CLI runtime (worktrees, CLAUDE.local.md); no dual-runtime fork is authored here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Load-bearing platform feature needs no fallback
rules_evaluated.evidence: The worktree/session mechanic is inherited from M4/M5 packaging, not newly introduced in this file; that platform decision was made upstream.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Eval architecture partition by evidence source
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule governs how eval judges are architected, not a property of a content file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Plug points are integration commitments; UX walk-through
rules_evaluated.evidence: L165 plug point 'Sponsor-stated or team-stated code-review conventions (feeds Phase 2 judge's quality bar, if the shape picked is LLM-judge)' references an 'LLM-judge' shape and 'Phase 2 judge's quality bar' that do not exist anywhere in this file's actual Phase 2 body (a stack-scan + diagram exercise, no judge construct). The bullet appears to be a stale/mismatched carry-over, so it fails the diagnostic ('point to sentence where YOUR context lands') — nothing in Phase 2 as written consumes a code-review convention.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either cut this plug point or rewrite it to name where sponsor code-review conventions would actually land in the current Phase 2 (e.g., as a category the stack-scan should recognise), since no LLM-judge shape exists in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test, 3 observable Monday outcomes
rules_evaluated.evidence: L152-155 three named-verb leap tests present: 'holds a diagrammed map...', 'cuts a stale rule...', 'reads a run's gaps as a ranked list...' — all observable actions, not abstract competencies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-phase failure mode + escape hatch
rules_evaluated.evidence: L156-160 names failure mode + diagnostic/escape for the diff (generalised diff), the packaging over-credit, the wider-look sprawl (covers the study+shapes forcing functions), and the rule-cut dodge — covering every forcing function's phase.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heavy fan-out prompts get body recovery callout, both directions
rules_evaluated.evidence: The Phase 2 study prompt (L64) is a textbook heavy fan-out prompt (§48 signal list names 'cross-project ~/.claude/projects/ session scans' and 'full-history audits' explicitly, both present here). Its body callouts at L58-60 ('Fast operator?' and 'Cut the scan when the top patterns are clear enough') only cover the OVER-reading direction. Neither callout names the premature-stop failure (a shallow pass declared done, or a confident-but-early-quit answer) that §48 requires to be named explicitly.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add a short body line before or after the study prompt naming the premature-stop risk and its recovery, e.g. nudging the student to say 'there's more here, keep going' if Claude's scan looks shallow — mirroring the existing over-reading callout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Save belongs with authoring, not loading
rules_evaluated.evidence: No create-then-use pair (author-and-load, build-and-run) spans this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Convenience-driven prompts get bias acknowledgment callout
rules_evaluated.evidence: No prompt in this file trades known shape-bias (self-charity, niceness-tax, overwrite-ambiguity) for convenience; none of the prompts fit this pattern.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Deliberate-antipattern prompts are class-judge exempt
rules_evaluated.evidence: No prompt in this file is engineered to deliberately exhibit a behavioral risk as the teaching moment (the M4-un-packaged baseline already ran in an earlier module).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Widgets carry semantics, match meaning not loudness

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise lead-in trio, three slots three tenses, ~15-word budget

rules_evaluated.evidence: L29-33 'Read the contrast, push back...' sits AFTER prompt 1, in legitimate post-action recap/coaching position; pre-prompt framing (L21-23) names artifact/coordinates/constraint only, never previews what the diff will reveal.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Engineer-audience audit fixes default to body callout
rules_evaluated.evidence: L44-47 'Say go, unless the cut spreads...' is a body callout (not a new forced prompt) for a recoverable-in-under-a-minute miss, matching the AE101 default.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Multi-session mechanic ships as packaging, not new primitive

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: /clear = tool, not ceremony
rules_evaluated.evidence: No /clear guidance is authored or required in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inbound links preserve pedagogical beat across reference restructuring

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Scan at the unit the rule names

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify mechanism before proposing surgery
rules_evaluated.evidence: Process rule governing an author proposing skill/framework changes; not testable against finished body content.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Acting on a flagged item — verify before fixing
rules_evaluated.evidence: Process rule for how auditors/maintainers should treat flagged items; not a content property of this file.

rules_evaluated.evidence: L31 'If Claude writes "the agent drifted on goal" without naming which commit... re-run the prompt with the quote rule re-asserted' is a generalizable steering move (recognize under-specificity, reassert the quote requirement), not a callout pinned to one prompt mechanic that would rot if the prompt's wording changes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Persistent TODO surfaces stale by default
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule governs how auditors treat long-lived punchlists; not a property this exercise's body exhibits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer blocks point, don't restate

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cross-module prerequisite rescue: run late, never fabricate
rules_evaluated.evidence: L7 handles only the thin/stalled-artefact grade ('M5's session may still be running the re-send. Leave it if that is the right call...'). No branch addresses the ABSENT-artefact grade (student never ran M5 at all), which the rule requires as a distinct rescue: running the missing module for real, compressed, trailing the room.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add a one-line body branch (or maintainer pointer to trainer-guide.md if it's covered there) for the case where M5 was skipped entirely, especially since AE101 also supports self-study delivery with no trainer to catch this in the room.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Three-pass build discipline
rules_evaluated.evidence: Process rule about generation-pass sequencing across ALL modules; not verifiable or applicable against one finished, already-shipped file.
